---
title: "What a p-value Actually Tells You"
date: 2026-07-01
categories: [statistics, hypothesis testing]
description: "A plain-language look at the most misunderstood number in applied research."
---

A p-value answers one narrow question: *if the null hypothesis were true, how surprising
is data this extreme or more extreme?* It is not the probability that the null hypothesis
is true, and it is not the probability that your result happened by chance.

A few things worth remembering when reporting or reading p-values:

- **Statistical significance is not practical significance.** A tiny effect can be
  "significant" with a large enough sample.
- **p < 0.05 is a convention, not a law of nature.** Treat it as one piece of evidence,
  not a verdict.
- **Report effect sizes and confidence intervals alongside p-values** — the magnitude
  and uncertainty usually matter more than the threshold.
